name: Strategy intake — Handy Set Go marketing agent
purpose: Turn raw facts about a company into the strategy document this app stores for a client. Everything the agent writes — campaigns, the schedule, the copy on each slot — reads from that document, so it is the source of truth and worth getting right.
how_to_use: 1. Fill in `company_input` below with whatever you know about the company. Blanks are fine — say 'unknown' rather than inventing.
2. Paste this whole file into ChatGPT along with anything else you have: the website, a deck, a sales call transcript, competitor pages, real customer quotes.
3. ChatGPT returns ONE JSON object matching `output.schema` — nothing else, no prose, no code fence.
4. Paste that object into the client's Strategy page in the app, or PUT it to /api/v1/clients/{clientId}/strategy.
task: You are a positioning and brand-voice strategist. Read `company_input` and any material the user pastes alongside it, then produce the strategy JSON described in `output`. Work from evidence: prefer the company's own words, its customers' words, and observable facts over generic marketing language. Where `company_input` is thin, say so in the field rather than filling the gap with something plausible-sounding — an honest blank is more useful than a confident guess, because a human reviews this before it drives anything. Before you answer, ask up to five clarifying questions if the answers would materially change the positioning; otherwise answer directly.

company_input._note: Fill this in. Free text everywhere — no formatting rules. 'unknown' is a valid answer.

basics.how_they_make_money: pricing model, typical deal size, one-off vs recurring
basics.geography: where they operate and where they sell

customers.who_buys: the person, not the company — job title, situation, what their day looks like
customers.who_they_do_NOT_serve: just as important as who they do
customers.best_customers: describe two or three real ones, by type
customers.why_customers_came: the moment that made them start looking
customers.how_customers_describe_the_problem: their words, verbatim if you have them — from calls, reviews, emails, support tickets

offer.what_changes_for_the_customer: the before and the after, concretely
offer.how_it_works: the mechanism — the actual thing they do differently
offer.proof: numbers, results, named clients, certifications, guarantees, years, volume
offer.objections_heard: what people say right before they don't buy

voice_and_brand.samples: paste two or three things they have published that sound right
voice_and_brand.words_they_use: industry terms, product names, phrases the founder repeats
voice_and_brand.formality: how a customer would expect to be spoken to
voice_and_brand.any_compliance_limits: regulated claims, disclaimers, things legal will not allow

goals_and_capacity.what_success_looks_like: the number that would make this quarter a win
goals_and_capacity.current_channels: where they already post, and what already works
goals_and_capacity.who_can_actually_make_content: who films, who designs, who approves
goals_and_capacity.realistic_output_per_week: be honest — a quota nobody can meet is worse than a small one
goals_and_capacity.seasonality: busy months, dead months, deadlines their customers care about

reference._note: The app validates against these. Values outside them are dropped on save.

post.label: Post
post.what: Text or single image. The default unit on every channel.

carousel.label: Carousel
carousel.what: Multi-slide. Carries a sequence — steps, myths, a breakdown.

reel.label: Reel
reel.what: Short vertical video. Needs a script and a shoot.

story.label: Story
story.what: Vertical, disappears in 24h. Behind-the-scenes and prompts.

thread.label: Thread
thread.what: A sequence of posts making one argument.

newsletter.label: Newsletter
newsletter.what: Long-form to the list. Usually the week's best idea, expanded.

post_alt.label: Alt post
post_alt.what: A second angle on the same theme, for testing.

retired_content_types._note: Do NOT put these in content_quota.weekly. A hook and a CTA are now part of every piece, not separate scheduled items.

demographic_fields._note: The editor renders these eight as named inputs. Extra keys are allowed and show as custom fields; keys are snake_case.
demographic_fields.industry: The sector they work in or buy for.
demographic_fields.age_range: Only when it genuinely segments the audience.
demographic_fields.language: The language they want to be sold in.
demographic_fields.income_or_revenue: Household income for a consumer, revenue for a business.

positioning_angle_types._note: Use one of these strings as `type`. Pick the one the evidence actually supports.
positioning_angle_types.contrarian: Challenge what everyone in the category believes.
positioning_angle_types.unique_mechanism: Lead with HOW it works, not what it is.
positioning_angle_types.transformation: The before and the after — the gap closed.
positioning_angle_types.enemy: Position against a common villain the customer already resents.
positioning_angle_types.speed_ease: Compress the time or reduce the effort it takes.
positioning_angle_types.specificity: Hyper-specific about who it is for and what it does.
positioning_angle_types.social_proof: Lead with the evidence, not the claim.

scheduling_ceiling._note: The planner places at most 2 pieces a day. A weekly quota totalling more than 14 can never be met and shows as a permanent shortfall on every Coverage row, which buries the real warnings. Set the quota to what the team can actually produce, not to what is theoretically ideal.

rules: Return one JSON object and nothing else. No markdown fence, no commentary before or after.
Use exactly the keys in output.schema. Extra keys are ignored by the app; missing keys are left untouched on save, so send every key you have an answer for.
Every string is plain text. No markdown, no emoji, no line breaks inside a value.
Arrays hold short standalone phrases — one idea each, no numbering, no trailing punctuation.
Write in the company's language, not marketing language. If a sentence could sit on any competitor's site unchanged, it is not positioning — rewrite it.

Banned words, always: revolutionary, game-changing, crushing it, leverage, synergy, unlock, seamless, cutting-edge, best-in-class, delve, landscape, paradigm, tapestry, elevate, empower, robust, holistic.
Claims need backing. If `company_input.offer.proof` does not support a number, do not use a number.
content_strategy is TOP LEVEL, a sibling of goals — not nested inside it.
content_quota.weekly keys must come from reference.content_types. Each entry's channels must be a subset of that type's allowed channels.
Leave a field as "" or [] when the input genuinely does not say. Do not pad.

output.format: A single JSON object. This is the exact body of PUT /api/v1/clients/{clientId}/strategy.

business_name.guidance: The trading name as customers write it. Required — a strategy cannot be created without it.

icp._what: Who this is for. The planner and the copy writer both read this to decide who they are talking to.

description.guidance: Two or three sentences describing one person, not a segment. Their role, their situation, what is on their plate this week.
description.example: Owner-operators of home service businesses doing $500k to $3M a year, usually 3 to 15 crew. They still answer the phone themselves. Growth has stalled not because demand dried up but because scheduling and follow-up eat the day.

demographics.guidance: Flat key/value. Use the eight keys in reference.demographic_fields — the editor renders those as named inputs. Leave a key out when it does not apply (company_size for a consumer product, age_range for B2B). You may add extra keys for a dimension only this company has; they appear as custom fields. Use snake_case.

pain_points.guidance: In their words. What actually hurts, not what the product fixes.
example: Quotes sit unanswered for days because nobody has time to chase them
Double-booked crews and no way to see it coming

desired_outcomes.guidance: What the customer is trying to achieve, independent of your product. Named `desired_outcomes` rather than `goals` because the top-level `goals` section means the MARKETING goals — a different thing.
example: Take on more jobs without hiring another office person

objections.guidance: What they say right before they don't buy.
example: We already pay for software nobody uses

trigger_events.guidance: The events that make someone start looking. These drive campaign timing.
example: Lost a big job to a competitor who quoted same-day

voice._what: How it sounds. The review engine checks generated copy against words_to_use and words_to_avoid, so these two lists do real work — make them specific.

personality.guidance: One or two sentences. If the brand were a person in the room, who?
personality.example: The experienced operator who has seen this before and tells you straight, without making you feel stupid for asking.

tone.guidance: The register — how formal, how warm, how much humour.
tone.example: Plainspoken and calm. Never salesy, never chummy. Short sentences.

communication_style.guidance: Structural habits: sentence length, whether it opens with a question, uses numbers, tells stories.
communication_style.example: Leads with the concrete situation, then the point. Uses real numbers over adjectives. No rhetorical questions as openers.

words_to_use.guidance: Actual vocabulary from the industry and the founder — terms of art, product names, phrases customers say.

words_to_avoid.guidance: Include the generic AI/marketing words AND anything specific to this brand.

positioning._what: Why them and not someone else. This is the highest-leverage section — campaigns inherit the angle.

fields.statement: One sentence a customer would recognise as true. No hedging.
fields.why: Why this angle works for THIS company — the evidence behind it.

example.statement: Every quote goes out the same day, because the estimate is written on site before the van leaves.
example.why: Their close rate is 3x on same-day quotes and competitors average four days. The mechanism is the differentiator, not the software.

secondary_angles.guidance: Two to four. Same shape as primary_angle; the app's editor shows type and statement, `why` is stored but not displayed. Genuinely different angles, not restatements of the primary.

example.statement: Built for people who already tried the all-in-one platform and went back to a whiteboard.
example.why: Every discovery call mentions an abandoned platform by name.

anti_positioning.guidance: Who this is explicitly NOT for, and what it deliberately does not do. Say it plainly — this is what makes the rest credible.
anti_positioning.example: Not for national franchises or anyone with a dedicated ops team. No inventory, no accounting, no payroll.

differentiation.guidance: The concrete difference versus the named alternatives, as a customer would verify it.
differentiation.example: Competitors sell a platform and charge for onboarding. Setup here is one afternoon and the price does not change with headcount.

messaging._what: The reusable lines. The copy writer pulls from here rather than reinventing the pitch on every post.

tagline.guidance: Under ten words. Says what it is, not how it feels.

value_props.guidance: Three to five. Each names an outcome the customer gets, not a feature you shipped.
example: Quote on site before you leave the driveway

key_messages.guidance: Three to six sentences that can be repeated across a quarter without wearing out. These become content pillars in practice.
example: The job is won or lost in the first 24 hours after the call

proof_points.guidance: Only what is verifiable. Numbers, named customers, guarantees, years, volume. If the input has none, return an empty array — do not invent.
example: Used by 40 home service businesses across 12 states

goals._what: What the marketing is for. Keeps the agent from optimising for the wrong thing.

secondary.example: Grow the email list to 2,000 owner-operators

focus_90_days.example: Establish the same-day quote mechanism as the thing they are known for, ahead of the spring busy season.

content_strategy._what: TOP LEVEL — a sibling of goals, not inside it. The planner reads platforms to know where things can go, and content_pillars to keep a month from becoming seven versions of the same post.

platforms.guidance: Where they will actually publish. Should line up with the channels used in content_quota.

content_pillars.guidance: Three to five recurring themes. Each should be able to carry a month of content on its own.
example: The first 24 hours after the call

content_quota._what: How much to publish per week and where. The planner uses this to find gaps in the calendar and place each piece.

weekly.type: object of content_type_key -> { count: number, channels: string[] }
weekly.guidance: Keys from reference.content_types only. Channels must be a subset of that type's allowed channels. Total count must not exceed 14 (2 a day) — and should match what the team can genuinely produce, from company_input.goals_and_capacity.realistic_output_per_week.

rationale.guidance: One short paragraph explaining the mix — why these formats, why this volume, what capacity it assumes. Shown to the operator above the quota table.
rationale.example: Five pieces a week, weighted to LinkedIn where the owner already has an audience. One carousel because the same-day quote mechanism needs steps to land. The newsletter carries the week's best idea. No Reels until someone can reliably film.

example_output._note: Shape reference only — a complete, valid payload. Do not copy the content.

objections: We already pay for software nobody uses

voice.communication_style: Concrete situation first, then the point. Numbers over adjectives.
